request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, a 73-year-old male, was admitted to the Urology ward with a chief complaint of nocturia, frequency, dribbling, and urinary retention since last month. Ultrasound examination revealed left renal mass. Past medical history included diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease. The patient stopped cigarette smoking 20 years ago. The lab data reveals that the patient had mild anemia and his blood sugar was 159 mg/dl. Urine analysis showed 10-15 white blood cells in high power field with a negative urine culture. Digital rectal examination showed a nodular (2-3+) and symmetric prostate. The ultrasound examination showed mild bilateral hydroureteronephrosis with an over-distended urinary bladder. The prostatic volume was 25 cc with retained urine of 950 cc. Computer tomography scanning revealed a hypo attenuated mass in the lower pole of the left kidney with arterial and portal enhancement and delay washout in favor of infiltrative process such as RCC close to left psoas muscle. Mild bilateral hydronephrosis due to enlarged prostate was seen. He was subsequently referred to the surgery department of the hospital for nephrectomy. The specimen was referred to the pathology department. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up:
After surgery, the patient was followed-up for 5 months. No recurrence or metastasis was diagnosed.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: C64**

The episode's main focus after investigation was the left renal mass, which was referred for nephrectomy. The follow-up for recurrence and metastasis points to a confirmed malignancy, most likely renal cell carcinoma, which falls under C64 (malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis). The urinary retention and enlarged prostate were real and needed management, but they were secondary to the renal condition that drove the surgical admission. The diagnosis section is withheld, so this is inferred from the clinical course rather than a stated diagnosis.
